Understanding pedagogical challenges faced by technology teachers in special needs classrooms
abstract: <jats:p>Teaching learners with special educational needs requires dynamic and adaptive pedagogical strategies that can lead to social development and academic success. This can be possible if teachers are assisted in mitigating the daily challenges of teaching such learners. This qualitative exploratory case study investigated the pedagogical challenges encountered by two Grade 9 Technology teachers in the Capricorn District of Limpopo Province. This study used Shulman’s Content and Pedagogical Knowledge framework to understand teachers’ challenges. Data was collected through semi-structured interviews and classroom observations; all collected data were analysed thematically. This study found that teachers experienced various challenges, including the emotional labour of teaching, burnout in the LSEN environment and the enactment of instructional knowledge. The study concluded that the sampled teachers displayed weaknesses in lesson planning, activating learners’ prior knowledge, diagnosing errors, achieving curriculum objectives and sustaining engagement. As a result, it was recommended that support through teacher assistants, creative differentiated strategies and enhanced digital-technology literacy to improve outcomes for learners with special needs was imminent.</jats:p>
venue: Journal of Education and Learning Technology
ai_summary: Teaching learners with special educational needs requires dynamic and adaptive pedagogical strategies . This can be possible if teachers are assisted in mitigating the daily challenges of teaching such learners .

Integration of Biomechanics and Digital Technology: Using Kinovea for Motion Analysis and Learning for Beginner Athletes
abstract:
<jats:p>Background: The integration of biomechanics with digital motion-analysis technologies has introduced new approaches for examining movement efficiency, kinematic characteristics, and technical patterns in walking and running activities. Kinovea, as an accessible motion-analysis software, provides both visual and quantitative feedback. However, its application in supporting technique development among beginner athletes remains insufficiently explored.
Aim: This study aims to describe the use of Kinovea in biomechanics training and examine its contribution to the awareness of kinematic characteristics and movement techniques among beginner athletes.
Methods: A descriptive qualitative design involved 72 beginner athletes aged 18–25 years selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected over 16 weeks through interviews, field observations, and motion video recordings analyzed using Kinovea. Kinematic data focused on joint angles, stride behavior, and movement phases during walking, running, and the flight phase. Qualitative data were analyzed using content analysis with NVivo 12, while kinematic results were interpreted descriptively to identify performance patterns and areas for technical refinement.
Result: Kinematic analysis showed coordinated joint-angle patterns across all phases. Walking analysis identified arm swing angles of 50.9°–58.8° and leg separation angles of 64.3°–67.2°, indicating a stable gait rhythm. The running analysis revealed knee angles of 68.8°–69.8° and elbow angles of 87.6°–89.1°, indicating efficient propulsive mechanics. The flight phase demonstrated knee angles of 81.2°–87.8° and elbow angles of 80.4°–88.3°, suggesting effective momentum use and postural stability. These measurements supported stride-efficiency assessment and technique evaluation. Qualitative findings revealed that Kinovea enabled athletes to interpret movement phases and identify technical inefficiencies through slow-motion and frame-by-frame visualization.
Conclusion: Kinovea supports basic motion analysis by providing clear kinematic information and helping beginner athletes observe and refine their movement techniques. The findings also offer practical value for coaches by enabling more precise identification of inefficient patterns and guiding targeted corrections during early-stage training.</jats:p>
venue: Journal of Coaching and Sports Science

HYBRID NETWORK INTRUSION DETECTION SYSTEM BASED ON SIGNATURE ANALYSIS AND MACHINE LEARNING METHODS
abstract: <jats:p>In the context of increasing complexity of modern network infrastructures and the growing number of cyberattacks, improving the effectiveness of intrusion detection systems is a highly relevant task. The aim of this work is to develop and investigate a hybrid approach to network attack detection based on a combination of signature-based analysis and intelligent machine learning methods.  The research methods include analysis of requirements for anomaly detection systems, comparative analysis of existing solutions, design of a hybrid system architecture, and experimental modeling using multiclass classification of network traffic. The results demonstrate that integrating a neural model with a traditional detection system improves attack detection coverage and reduces the number of false positives.  The practical significance of the study lies in the possibility of deploying the proposed architecture in real corporate networks, while the theoretical significance consists in substantiating the effectiveness of a hybrid approach to traffic analysis. Future research directions include adaptive model training and expansion of the range of detectable attacks.</jats:p>

title: A Review of Phishing Detection Techniques Using Machine Learning and Natural Language Processing
abstract: <jats:p>The goal of phishing attacks, which rank high among cyber risks, is to steal sensitive information (such as login passwords, financial data, and more) from unsuspecting people and companies. Blacklist, whitelist, rule, heuristic, and signature-based detection methods are no longer suitable due to the rising sophistication of phishing schemes. As a result, ML, DL, and NLP are rapidly becoming into effective instruments for detecting both well-known and brand-new forms of phishing. Background on phishing assaults, old ways of detecting them, and recent advances in intelligent phishing detection are all included in this article. It delves into several machine learning algorithms such as decision tree, LSTM, ANN, CNN, and RNN, as well as deep learning models like KNN, NB, and SVM. Also, natural language processing methods including word embedding, sentiment analysis, text categorization, and tokenization are explored with the aim of detecting phishing material. Presenting a comprehensive, precise, and up-to-the-minute phishing detection system is the ultimate goal of this study, which focuses on machine learning frameworks, performance indicators, present obstacles, and future research directions.</jats:p>
venue: Journal of Global Research in Multidisciplinary Studies(JGRMS)
ai_summary: ML, DL, and NLP are rapidly becoming into effective instruments for detecting both well-known and brand-new forms of phishing . Background on phishing assaults and old ways of detecting them are all included in this article .

Thinking out of distribution: what a PhD must train in the age of AI.
abstract: The production of scientific knowledge, as well as the skills required for research, is undergoing profound changes in the age of Artificial Intelligence (AI) assisted research. At the same time, the use of AI assistants has been linked to the atrophy of some skills among students at different levels. Doctoral students are in a particular position: in previous levels of higher education, students' role is based on acquiring skills; doctoral education, however, is centered on mastering knowledge in a given field as well as on being able to produce novel scientific research. In this new scientific landscape, this means balancing learning fundamental skills (e.g., formulating interesting scientific questions, articulating assumptions) with learning how to work proficiently and reliably using modern tools. While the tools that are used will keep changing, we believe that the core objective of doctoral training remains unchanged: preparing the next generation of scientists to continue the human scientific endeavor.
ai_summary: The production of scientific knowledge is undergoing profound changes in the age of Artificial Intelligence . The use of AI assistants has been linked to the atrophy of some skills among students at different levels .

title: Recommendations for Incorporating Large Language Models Into Psychological Research: A Commentary on Austin et al. (2025).
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have clear potential to contribute to psychological research methods. However, as with any new research method, LLM-based methods require rigorous evaluation. Towards this end, Austin and colleagues evaluated the ability of two LLMs (GPT-4o and Gemini 2.0 Flash) to facilitate scale validation by identifying relevant criterion measures and generating validity hypotheses for assessing convergent and discriminant validity. We argue that their study has several key limitations that limit the conclusions that can be drawn about the proposed method's suitability for use in validation research. We situate our critique within three recommendations for incorporating LLMs into research: (a) avoid essentialisation and overgeneralisation about 'AI', (b) use application programming interfaces when evaluating LLMs in research contexts and (c) evaluate LLM-based methods using clearly specified criteria. Finally, we consider whether adopting the proposed method might reinforce or amplify existing limitations in the psychological literature, namely, the proliferation of overlapping constructs and inadequately validated measures.

Exploring Snake Species Diversity, Habitat Suitability, and Threats in Two Protected Forests of Southeastern Bangladesh Using Field Observations and Ensemble Learning.
abstract: This study aims to elucidate snake species richness, distribution patterns, habitat suitability and their conservation concern in Kaptai National Park (KNP) and Dudpukuria-Dhopachari Wildlife Sanctuary (DDWS), two biodiverse protected forests in Bangladesh's southeastern region. No comprehensive study of snakes in these two forests is available. By surveying 488.3 km through systematic transect sampling and opportunistic surveys, spending 1776 person-hours, we found 36 snake species (26 from KNP and 23 from DDWS) from 23 genera and eight families across the two study sites. Forest edge and hilly stream habitats exhibit the highest species richness and the most even species distributions at KNP. Whereas, DDWS revealed the highest species richness in hilly streams and waterlogged habitats, and greater evenness in forest edges and roadside vegetation. Habitat suitability models developed using Random Forest (for KNP) and Extreme Gradient Boosting (for DDWS) consistently identified climatic seasonality variables as the dominant predictors of snake distribution. Current suitability maps identified humid valley floors, riparian corridors, and evergreen hill forests as areas of high suitability in both protected areas. The habitat suitability model suggests that riparian corridors and moist evergreen forest patches should be well conserved to protect snakes from future changes. The findings significantly expand our understanding of snake species in two significant biodiversity-rich habitats, adding valuable information to national and global taxonomic databases and conservation planning efforts.
ai_summary: Study aims to elucidate snake species richness, distribution patterns, habitat suitability and conservation concern . No comprehensive study of snakes in these two forests is available . By surveying 488.3 km through systematic transect sampling and opportunistic surveys, we found 36 snake species .

title: Estimation of attributable fractions for time-to-event outcomes using an inverse probability weighted Kaplan-Meier estimator.
abstract: Population attributable fractions aim to quantify the proportion of the cases of an outcome (eg, a disease) that would have been avoided had no individuals in the population been exposed to a given exposure. This quantity thus plays a crucial role in epidemiology and public health, notably to guide policies, interventions, or to assess the burden of a disease due to a particular exposure. Various statistical methods have been proposed to estimate attributable fractions using observational data. When time-to-event data are used, several of these formulas yield invalid results. Alternative valid formulas are available but remain scarcely used. We propose a new estimator of the attributable fraction that is both conceptually simple and easy to implement using common statistical software. Our proposed estimator makes use of the Kaplan-Meier estimator to address censoring and potentially non-proportional hazards, as well as inverse probability weighting to control confounding. Non-parametric bootstrap is proposed to produce inferences. A simulation study is used to illustrate and compare our proposed estimator to several alternatives. The results showcase the bias of many commonly used traditional approaches and the validity of our estimator under its working assumptions.

title: Assessment of the conditional exchangeability assumption in causal machine learning models: a simulation study.
abstract: Observational studies developing causal machine learning models for prediction of individualized treatment effects (ITEs) seldom conduct empirical evaluations to assess the conditional exchangeability assumption. We conducted a simulation study to illustrate the performance of causal forest and X-learner models under conditional exchangeability violations, in the presence and absence of true heterogeneity, and to assess the utility of negative control outcomes (NCOs) as diagnostics. We simulated data to reflect real-world scenarios with differing levels of confounding, sample size, and NCO confounding structures, then estimated and compared ITE-defined strata treatment effects on the primary outcome and NCOs across settings with and without unmeasured confounding. When conditional exchangeability was violated, models failed to recover true treatment effect heterogeneity and, in some cases, falsely suggested heterogeneity when none existed. Negative control outcomes successfully identified strata affected by unmeasured confounding. Even when NCOs did not perfectly satisfy ideal assumptions, they flagged potential bias in estimates across ITE-defined strata, though not always pinpointing the stratum with the largest confounding. Violations of conditional exchangeability substantially limit the validity of ITE estimates in routinely collected observational data. Negative control outcomes serve as a useful empirical diagnostic tool for detecting unmeasured confounding that varies across subpopulations, helping to support the credibility of individualized inference.
ai_summary: Study looked at causal forest and X-learner models under conditional exchangeability violations . It found models failed to recover true treatment effect heterogeneity and falsely suggested heterogeneity when none existed .

title: A Bayesian latent class analysis approach for assessing the accuracy of natural language processing models classifying topic and sentiment of public health-related social media content.
abstract: Natural language processing (NLP) models can classify unstructured social media content into structured data suitable for generating public health intelligence. Natural language processing models, however, can vary in performance, given differences in architecture and sensitivities to temporal drift. Our objective was measuring the performance of different NLP models for identifying topics and sentiment of social media posts related to COVID-19 within a framework that integrated model outputs and human-labeled posts. Posts were obtained from Twitter (Canada; December 2020-August 2021). Tweets were classified by public health measure (PHM) topic (mask-wearing, vaccination, social distancing, others) using 5 crowdsourcing annotators, a keyword-based filter (KB), and a large language model (LLM). Sentiment (in support, neutral, against) was categorized using the same crowdsourcing annotators and LLM, and a neural network sentiment analysis (NSA) model. Sensitivity and specificity of the NLP models were estimated using hierarchical Bayesian latent class models. A total of 443 and 801 tweets were assessed for topic and sentiment classification, respectively. Keyword-based and LLM models had similar specificity and sensitivity for all topics, except for LLM having higher sensitivity for vaccination (0.88). The NSA model yielded sensitivity < 0.50 for classifying "in support" and "against" sentiments, while the LLM had sensitivity > 0.60 for all sentiments. Deployment of NLP models for public health applications requires critical understanding of model performance. This study demonstrates an approach to estimate the posterior distribution of the probability, adjusted for misclassification error, of including topic/sentiment for each social media post and derived classifier accuracy metrics for the tests.

title: ICD-10 code embedding for patient matching: a first step toward applications in causal inference from hospital discharge data.
abstract: We present WEMatch, a Word2vec Enhanced ICD-10 Matching algorithm, for patient matching based on ICD-10 codes and make a first step toward evaluating its potential use in causal inference contexts by comparing it to several propensity score-based patient matching approaches. We use hospital discharge data from the Insel Group in the canton of Bern, Switzerland, from 2014 to 2023, including ICD-10 codes, age, sex, and BMI for 386 842 hospitalizations. In the null-effect matched cohort design, patients are matched to a randomly selected "treatment group" (selected from 1 of 4 selected primary ICD-10 diagnoses) using 4 algorithms: WEMatch and 3 propensity score matching (PSM)-based models. Performance is assessed by comparing the balance of key variables, hazard ratios of mortality, and length of hospital stay between the treatment and matched control groups. WEMatch and PSM methods perform similarly for 3 out of 4 tested ICD-10 codes. For one ICD-10 code, WEMatch outperforms PSM methods, because the patient population is especially diverse. This study establishes a robust framework for systematically comparing patient matching algorithms. The groundwork is set for applying WEMatch to clinically relevant questions. By distributing this as an R package, we promote its integration into clinical research, potentially supporting future causal analyses using observational data.

title: Estimating the causal effect of sugar consumption on dental decay: a longitudinal targeted maximum likelihood estimation study.
abstract: Dental decay in permanent teeth is the most prevalent disease worldwide, with 54% of young people under the age of 18 having experienced it. Despite these findings, there have been no studies that investigated the causal effects of time-varying exposure to higher sugar consumption throughout childhood on dental decay in late adolescence. We investigated the causal effects of sustained higher sugar consumption, cumulative sugar consumption, and sugar consumption trajectories from ages 4 to 14 on the risk of ever experiencing dental decay at age 16. We used data from the Longitudinal Study of Australian Children, an ongoing national Australian study that started in 2004, with a sample of 4671 young people. Causal effects were estimated using longitudinal targeted maximum likelihood estimation combined with the Super Learner ensemble. Young people with sustained higher sugar consumption (ie, above-median sugar consumption at ages 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, and 14) throughout the study period had a 37 percentage point higher risk of dental decay compared to those with no exposure. Each additional exposure to higher sugar consumption (ie, additional above-median sugar consumption at a certain age) between ages 4 and 14 was associated with a 6% increase in the relative risk of dental decay by age 16. This study provides causal evidence linking higher sugar consumption throughout childhood to dental decay in late adolescence.
ai_summary: 54% of young people under the age of 18 have experienced dental decay . No studies have investigated the causal effects of time-varying exposure to higher sugar consumption throughout childhood .

title: Beyond just survival: updates on adult congenital heart disease care.
abstract: Survival into adulthood is now the norm for individuals born with congenital heart disease, with over 90% of children reaching adult life. Yet for many, particularly those with complex lesions, childhood intervention does not equate to a cure. Adults with congenital heart disease (ACHD) face ongoing risks of haemodynamic complications, end-organ dysfunction, and premature morbidity. In this review, we present recent advances in ACHD care across five domains: lifelong care models, diagnostic techniques, management strategies, genetic and precision medicine, and machine learning. We highlight the pivotal role of specialized, multidisciplinary care in improving outcomes, and the need for structured transition programmes to ensure continuity from paediatric to adult services. Emerging priorities include reproductive counselling, exercise prescription, and psychosocial support. Advances in cardiovascular magnetic resonance imaging, electrophysiological mapping, and four-dimensional flow imaging now offer unprecedented anatomical and haemodynamic insights. Recent trials have demonstrated encouraging results for novel heart failure therapies and pulmonary vasodilators in lesion-specific subgroups, while transcatheter technologies continue to expand therapeutic options for patients with complex anatomy. Genetic testing and machine learning are beginning to reshape risk stratification and workflow efficiency, though challenges remain in their implementation. As this population ages and acquires new comorbidities, care models must evolve to move beyond just survival, but towards improving quality of life, preserving organ function, and anticipating future needs. This review aims to support clinicians and researchers in meeting these challenges and advancing the next era of ACHD care.
venue: European heart journal. Valvular and structural heart disease
ai_summary: Adults with congenital heart disease face ongoing risks of haemodynamic complications, end-organ dysfunction, and premature morbidity . In this review, we present recent advances in ACHD care across five domains .
